segments.narration: This war started at 9:02 and ended at 9:40. Zanzibar, 27 August 1896.
Two days earlier the pro-British sultan died. His nephew Khalid bin Barghash seized the palace before Britain could install its own man.
Britain's ultimatum was blunt: be out by nine in the morning. Khalid barricaded himself inside with thousands of defenders and waited to see if Britain meant it.
Why would anyone hold a wooden palace against a modern fleet? At 9:02 two cruisers and three gunboats opened fire from the harbour.

By 9:40 the palace flag was down. Khalid ran for the German consulate, Britain crowned its chosen sultan that afternoon, and roughly five hundred Zanzibaris were killed or wounded inside thirty-eight minutes.
